# Dependabot skips weekends, so releases shipped on Saturday or Sunday wait until Monday

## Context

`.github/dependabot.yml` schedules both ecosystems (npm, github-actions) with `interval: daily`, which Dependabot runs Monday to Friday only. The dynamic `npm_and_yarn in /.` job ran at 07:31Z on Oct 28–30 and Nov 2–6, with no runs on Oct 31, Nov 1, Nov 7 or Nov 8. `neo-agent-skills` ships one or more versions a day, weekends included: v0.1.94 came out on Fri Nov 6 at 16:22Z, after that day's run, and 1.0.0 and 1.1.0 came out on Sun Nov 8. The Engine therefore stays on a skills version several releases old until Monday, and every Engine seat reads that older protocol. The operator asked for weekends to be included (2026-11-08).

## The Problem

A weekday-only schedule leaves up to 3 days of skills releases uninstalled, and the gap is widest exactly when the team works through a weekend.

## The Architectural Reality

- Design authority: n/a — this changes a schedule and calls no behaviour wrong.
- Dependabot supports a cron schedule: `schedule.interval: cron` with `schedule.cronjob: "<expression>"`.
- The file's other policies stay as they are: majors are included, cooldown 3 days with `neo-agent-skills` excluded, and grouping.

## The Fix

Both ecosystems switch from `interval: daily` to `interval: cron` with `cronjob: "30 7 * * *"`, every day at the same morning hour as today. A one-line header note says why `daily` was not enough.

Decision Record impact: none.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Both `schedule` blocks use `interval: cron` and `cronjob: "30 7 * * *"`; nothing else in the file changes.
- [ ] Post-merge: a Dependabot npm run appears on the next Saturday or Sunday.

## Out of Scope

Grouping, cooldown and the majors policy. The Brain and Institution repositories each own their own `dependabot.yml`.
